liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bertha** (2 reviews): Reviewer's all-time favorite Bertha; Jerry's mid-song solo is called perfect; The Bertha solo is said to have no equal [8][11]
- **Row Jimmy** (2 reviews): Reviewer says this Row Jimmy beats the 5/8/77 version, with Jerry's playing sounding like honey; Reviewer singles out Row Jimmy, along with Bertha and Passenger, as nice versions in a strong first set [8][16]
- **They Love Each Other** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the greatest version ever, with beautiful mid-song solos from Jerry and Keith [11]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The Scarlet>Fire medley is called a possible best of the year, with a note-perfect, smooth transition [16]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 review): Reviewer has never heard a better rocking Brown Eyed Women, from a crisp Betty-board tape [12]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): The reviewer's highlight is the jam that comes out of He's Gone [5]

## The recordings

- **gd77-05-21.sbd.boyle.271.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 186 min; rated 4.18/5 by 22 [1]. Said about its sound: The reviewer finds the soundboard download to be pretty good quality; The reviewer describes the recording's sound quality as excellent [5][6]
- **gd1977-05-21.157234.partial.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: audience recording; 9 songs; 85 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Very good recording, though the bottom end was extremely heavy and needed EQ [3]
- **gd1977-05-21.139573.sbd.gastwirt.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: soundboard; 24 songs; 185 min; rated 4/5 by 8 [2]
- **gd1977-05-21.157233.partial.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac16**: audience recording; 9 songs; 85 min [4]

## Around the show

- A listener who thinks it was their first show has a ticket stub reading 5-15-17 and wonders about postponement [13]
- Consistently good performances matching the pace of other May '77 shows, though not necessarily the best-ever versions [6]
- Reviewer calls it a contender for best show of 1977 and says it surpasses the Cornell show [7]
- Reviewer lists many songs here, including Scarlet>Fire, He's Gone and Comes a Time, as top-three versions of the year [8]
- Reviewer ranks it among the best May 1977 shows, with some of the year's finest moments [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-05-21.sbd.boyle.271.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Reviewer notes the Dick's Picks 29 release was the Atlanta show, not this Lakeland one; Source credited to D. Boyles; reportedly there may be two different .shn versions [1][14]
- **gd1977-05-21.157234.partial.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac24**: taped by From the tape collection of Doug Lamarre; transferred by Sirmick and Matt Vernon; source: Unknown audience recording (low gen) from the collection of Doug Lamarre. [3]. Also: Partial audience recording from Doug Lamarre, transferred by Matt Vernon, with a few patches from Rich Gastwirt's soundboard; speed corrected [3]
- **gd1977-05-21.139573.sbd.gastwirt.miller.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by From Gastwirt Collection; transferred by Charlie Miller and SIRMick; source: Source: sbd > master reel > dat (44.1k) - Provided by Rich Gastwirt; Transfer: Dat > Panasonic SV-3700 > Tascam DA-3000 . wav 16/44.1 - Transferred by Charlie… [2]
- **gd1977-05-21.157233.partial.aud.lamarre.vernon.sirmick.flac16**: taped by From the tape collection of Doug Lamarre; transferred by Sirmick and Matt Vernon; source: Unknown audience recording (low gen) from the collection of Doug Lamarre. [4]

## Art and photos

- Photo by Caine Schneider (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - Dick's Picks Vol. 29 (Lakeland 5/21/77)](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26793379911/) [18]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26793379911/) [19]
